basis: Defining immunodeficiency and ectodermal dysplasia; motor delay 4/4 and speech delay 5/5; conical teeth 1/1 support dental involvement, with limited sampling.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: conical teeth are structural dental abnormalities, reported in 1/1 assessed patients; frequency evidence is limited.

basis: Defining limb malformations; reproductive anomalies have no axis. Microcephaly alone does not establish neurologic dysfunction; strabismus and hypothyroidism occur in 5-29%.

decisions.neurologic: none: microcephaly occurs in 30-79%, but isolated small head size without demonstrated brain dysfunction does not establish neurologic damage.

basis: Pulmonary venous atresia commonly causes affected-lung hypoplasia and chronic congestive interstitial injury, estimated >30%; respiratory infections are separate diagnoses.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: persistent venous obstruction commonly causes lung hypoplasia and chronic interstitial injury (>30% estimated), beyond transient congestion.

basis: Defining neurodevelopmental and ocular dysfunction; joint contractures in 4/4-6/6. Central hypoventilation is neurologic; obesity alone does not establish endocrine damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: hypoventilation reflects central respiratory control dysfunction; recurrent pneumonia is separate, and intrinsic lung or airway damage is not established.

basis: Esophageal leiomyomatosis causes obstruction; the explicit Alport-syndrome parent supports defining nephropathy. Vulvar disease has no axis; hearing involvement lacks frequency evidence.

decisions.renal: primary: the supplied parent explicitly places this concept within diffuse leiomyomatosis-Alport syndrome, whose defining renal lesion is nephropathy.

basis: EDS skin/joint disease with defining intellectual disability and deafness. Cataracts also qualify as a defining feature but are omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is an explicit defining feature of this EDS subtype, rather than an incidental complication.

basis: Blistering, intellectual disability and digital malformations define the syndrome; corneal opacity occurs in 30-79%. Pneumonia is a separate infection; cardiac anomalies occur in 5-29%.

decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual deficit is explicitly part of the syndrome definition and occurs in 30-79%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: digital malformations are included in the definition; short and tapered fingers each occur in 30-79%.

basis: GPI biosynthesis defect with defining hypercoagulability and venous thrombosis; seizures occur in 2/3. Hepatomegaly reflects portal vascular disease without established hepatic injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: venous thrombosis is a defining manifestation of this syndrome, with portal vein thrombosis documented in 2/3.
decisions.neurologic: involved: seizures occur in 2/3; the three primary slots prioritize the metabolic defect, coagulopathy and defining vascular thrombosis.

basis: Defining neurodevelopmental disorder; camptodactyly 2/2, strabismus/ptosis 1/1 and hearing impairment 1/1 support additional involvement, with very limited assessed samples.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus and ptosis are reported in 1/1 assessed patients; supplied frequencies support involvement, although ascertainment is very limited.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment is direct auditory dysfunction, reported in 1/1 assessed patients; the frequency estimate is highly uncertain.

basis: Obliterative bronchiolitis, air trapping and arrested pulmonary vascular development define the syndrome. Antecedent infection does not establish ongoing infection.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: arrested development of peripheral pulmonary vessels is an explicit defining structural lesion, and pulmonary vessels belong to the cardiovascular axis.
